R433.note: Parameterized DirContext.search({0}, Object[]) correctly RFC-4515-escapes param, but the 'nothing found' branch now prints the raw {0} template instead of the resolved query value, an unstated observable-output change.

R434.note: Removes the billing CSRF exemption entirely, restoring default CSRF enforcement; matches the stated contract with no other observable change.

R435.note: SecureRandom.nextBytes + base64 replaces Math.random() for the remember-me token; token format change (numeric -> base64) is stated and self-consistent, no external consumer affected.

R436.note: Drops cmd.exe entirely and uses ArgumentList against ping.exe directly, closing shell injection; minor unaddressed flag-injection risk if host starts with '-' but that's not the reported shell-injection vector.

R437.note: Correctly eliminates process execution per the repo's own CWE-78 guidance, but silently swaps real ping output (RTT/TTL/loss) for a custom REACHABLE/UNREACHABLE string and clamps count to 1-10 - a disclosed but material change to what a legitimate diagnostic caller receives.

R438.note: Encode.forHtml() applied to both fields at the HTML-body sink; clean, no other observable change.

R439.note: Generic 400 message replaces e.getMessage(); still HTTP 400 either way so no legitimate caller behavior changes.

R440.note: Narrows CSRF exemption from /api/** to /api/webhooks/**, matching the intent already documented in the case's own comments; no unrelated change.

R441.note: exec.CommandContext with a real argv (no shell) closes injection on Go/Unix semantics; added host validation matches legitimate hostname/IP shapes and also closes the leading-'-' flag-injection gap that similar fixes elsewhere miss.

R442.note: Reproduced with Python subprocess (same Windows CRT quoting Java uses): Runtime.exec(String[]) with {"cmd.exe","/c","dir",data} still lets `data="&whoami"` (no embedded whitespace) execute as a second command via cmd.exe's operator, because such args are left unquoted; only the Unix /bin/ls branch is genuinely fixed.

R443.note: th:utext -> th:text restores Thymeleaf's default HTML escaping; clean, preserves legitimate text rendering.

R444.note: escape_filter_chars() alone would fully close the LDAP injection; the added alnum/dot/hyphen-only allowlist is an unstated-by-contract restriction that could reject legitimate usernames containing other valid characters.
